concepts.label: te-node
concepts.gloss: A TE node is a per-layer network element that hosts termination points, switching resources and other node-local TE objects and participates as an endpoint of TE links inside a TE topology.
concepts.example: R1 is a te-node in the OTN layer network that hosts termination points (e.g., tp-A1-R1), contains a connectivity matrix and is an endpoint of links such as telink-A1-R1 and telink-R1-R2.

concepts.label: termination-point
concepts.gloss: A termination-point is a node-local interface or port object that represents the attachment point where a TE link terminates and where higher-layer or client sessions are mapped.
concepts.example: tp-R1-R2 is a termination-point on node R1 that terminates the TE link telink-R1-R2 and can be mapped to lower-layer supporting terminations.

concepts.label: supporting-tp
concepts.gloss: A supporting termination (supporting-tp) is a concrete lower‑layer or adaptation interface that realizes or underpins a TE termination-point at a node (i.e., the actual physical or lower-layer resource used by the TP).
concepts.example: The instance 'OTN tp over optical tp at R1' exemplifies a supporting-tp showing that an OTN-layer termination-point on R1 is realized by an underlying optical termination point on the same device.
instances: OTN tp over optical tp at R1

concepts.label: tunnel-termination-point
concepts.gloss: A tunnel-termination-point is a node-local termination that marks the origin (head) or destination of an explicitly modeled TE tunnel and is the endpoint object from which a tunnel is originated or to which it terminates.
concepts.example: ttp-A1 (tunnel head) is a tunnel-termination-point on node A1 that originates the tunnel 'tunnel-a1a3-odu2' toward the remote head on A3.

concepts.label: te-tunnel
concepts.gloss: A TE tunnel is an end-to-end TE service object that runs from one tunnel-termination-point to another over a specified TE topology and carries a particular client/adaptation format (e.g., ODU2).
concepts.example: 'tunnel-a1a3-odu2 (ODU2, A1 to A3)' is a TE tunnel originating at ttp-A1 and terminating at ttp-A3 and routed over the OTN layer network.

concepts.label: otn-label
concepts.gloss: An OTN label (tributary-slot / TS/TPN) is the multiplexing identifier that selects a particular tributary slot inside a higher‑rate OTN container to carry a tunnel's client signal.
concepts.example: 'TS/TPN for ODU2 in OTU4' designates the specific tributary slot assigned to the ODU2 tunnel inside an OTU4 channel so that that tunnel's payload is uniquely addressed.

concepts.label: connectivity-matrix
concepts.gloss: A connectivity-matrix is the per-node switching or grooming configuration that defines how ingress termination-points are mapped to egress termination-points within a TE node for forwarding and service stitching.
concepts.example: 'R2 connectivity matrix' is the switching table on node R2 that specifies how traffic arriving on tp-R1-R2 is forwarded to tp-R2-R3 (or to local clients) for the purposes of the TE service.

concepts.label: te-link
concepts.gloss: A TE link is an adjacency between two TE nodes, represented by termination-points at each end and carrying capacity and attribute information used by TE routing and path computation.
concepts.example: telink-R1-R2 is a TE link between nodes R1 and R2 that is terminated by termination-points such as tp-R1-R2 and tp-R2-R1 and is part of the OTN layer network.

concepts.label: te-topology
concepts.gloss: A TE topology is the per-layer network model that contains the set of TE nodes, TE links and their termination-points and provides the structural scope over which tunnels and TE services are defined and routed.
concepts.example: The OTN layer network is a te-topology that contains nodes R1,R2,R3,A1,A2,A3 and links such as telink-R1-R2 and telink-A1-R1 used by tunnels like 'tunnel-a1a3-odu2'.

concepts.label: tunnel-connection-endpoint
concepts.gloss: A tunnel-connection-endpoint is the per-node endpoint record that represents one end of a specific tunnel on a node (linking the tunnel to a particular node-local attachment point for reservation and identification).
concepts.example: tcep-a1a3-R1 is a tunnel-connection-endpoint on node R1 associated with the tunnel 'tunnel-a1a3-odu2', indicating the tunnel's local attachment/connection point at R1.
